title: Power Rankings: Mavs still No. 1 to Dirk's surprise
heading: 2006-07 Power Rankings: Week 22
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: Actual quote from Dirk after Mavs were denied a single-season record fourth double-digit win streak: ''Are we down to No. 2?'' He seemed strangely surprised to hear no.
rankings.summaryText: Actual quote from Dirk after Mavs were denied a single-season record fourth double-digit win streak: ''Are we down to No. 2?'' He seemed strangely surprised to hear no.

rankings.summaryHtml: Suns are only 6-4 in their last 10 games. But when two of those Ws come against one of the foremost regular-season juggernauts of all time, committees like us notice.
rankings.summaryText: Suns are only 6-4 in their last 10 games. But when two of those Ws come against one of the foremost regular-season juggernauts of all time, committees like us notice.

rankings.summaryHtml: It doesn't feel great demoting Spurs after a 19-3 run secured a ninth straight 50-win season, No. 3 all time for such streaks. But Sunday's scores left us no choice.

rankings.summaryHtml: Like others before them, Jazz respond to a temporary drop to the cure-all No. 7 spot with a huge win in Houston. Utah is now a tidy 10-4 against the rest of the top six.
rankings.summaryText: Like others before them, Jazz respond to a temporary drop to the cure-all No. 7 spot with a huge win in Houston. Utah is now a tidy 10-4 against the rest of the top six.

rankings.summaryHtml: Pistons are still the only team in the league better on the road (24-13) than at home (23-13). They'll also be the East's only 50-win team unless Cavs or Bulls get hot.
rankings.summaryText: Pistons are still the only team in the league better on the road (24-13) than at home (23-13). They'll also be the East's only 50-win team unless Cavs or Bulls get hot.

rankings.summaryHtml: This could still be the first T-Mac team to get past Round 1, but chances are it won't be the first T-Mac team to have home-court advantage. Not after that Utah loss.
rankings.summaryText: This could still be the first T-Mac team to get past Round 1, but chances are it won't be the first T-Mac team to have home-court advantage. Not after that Utah loss.

rankings.summaryHtml: Cavs won the biggest game of their season Saturday. But they're 3-5 since March 17 and still could slip to No. 5 in the East, which might mean (gulp) Miami in Round 1.
rankings.summaryText: Cavs won the biggest game of their season Saturday. But they're 3-5 since March 17 and still could slip to No. 5 in the East, which might mean (gulp) Miami in Round 1.

rankings.summaryHtml: Even though Chicago has given Miami fits on a playoff stage, I'll go out on a limb and suggest Bulls would rather pass Cavs if they can to secure an easier first-round foe.

rankings.summaryHtml: The fairy tale continues: Raps seal their first playoff spot since '02 by beating Bobs on Sunday. Their magic number to clinch the first division title in club history is three.
rankings.summaryText: The fairy tale continues: Raps seal their first playoff spot since '02 by beating Bobs on Sunday. Their magic number to clinch the first division title in club history is three.

rankings.summaryHtml: Trivia time: How many times this season have Heat dressed their top eight players and their head coach? Answer: Once. The night D-Wade went down in Houston.

rankings.summaryHtml: Lakers are 20-8 when Kobe is joined by these three bigs in the lineup: Odom, Walton and Kwame Brown. But with so many injuries, Kobe's Lakers are just 19-23 in 2007.

rankings.summaryHtml: Surest sign yet that Clips have righted their slip and will reach the playoffs, with or without Cassell: Friday's victory was L.A.'s first in 18 games in Sacramento since 1997.

rankings.summaryHtml: The flipside to their road woes: Warriors have racked up more wins at home (27) than San Antonio (26) and all but three West teams: Mavs (33), Suns (31) and Jazz (29).

rankings.summaryHtml: Team with the toughest closing schedule loses the easiest game left on that schedule at home to Sonics. Double uh-oh: Nuggets are 2-5 since that five-game win streak.

rankings.summaryHtml: The division title was slipping away from Wiz even with Butler healthy. But losing the Wisconsin native in Milwaukee, probably 'til next season, was needlessly cruel.

rankings.summaryHtml: Grant Hill is playing in his first April since (gulp) 2000. He'd be in the midst of a clutch five-game winning streak, too, if Magic didn't lose both OT games last week.

rankings.summaryHtml: Falling upwards remains the most accurate description for Nets' playoff ''drive.'' They awoke Monday sitting seventh in the East despite a 6-9 record in March.

rankings.summaryHtml: If they don't seem so desperate for No. 8, maybe it's because Hornets have lost 21 games in a row to Dallas. There's no longer active drought in major US team sports.

rankings.summaryHtml: Pacers obviously can't post the 9-0 finish needed to avoid Carlisle's first-ever losing season. But if they can beat SA sans O'Neal, maybe the playoffs aren't out of reach.

rankings.summaryHtml: Isiah Contract Extension Update: Knicks lost four home games in March to sub-.500 teams (Sonics, Hornets, Blazers and Magic) to all but kill their playoff fantasies.

rankings.summaryHtml: Stubborn Sixers were never going to rally all the way into the playoffs, but they do still have a better record since the Iverson trade than Denver at 24-26 to Nuggets' 22-27.

rankings.summaryHtml: Playoff push? Since the All-Star break, only three teams have worse records than Wolves' 6-15 mark. They are: Indy at 4-17, Memphis at 5-16 and Atlanta at 6-16.

rankings.summaryHtml: With Pierce, Celts are a (virtually) respectable 20-27, on pace to go 35-47 over a full season. Without Pierce, Celts are 3-23, on pace to match the mythical 9-73 mark.
